name: Hamath
overview: Hamath is a male figure identified in Scripture as a son of Canaan. Beyond this unique attribute, there is no additional tribal affiliation or further notes recorded about him. His mention is brief, emphasizing his genealogical role within the descendants of Canaan.
namesAndTitles: The name Hamath appears as a proper name in the biblical record without any specific meaning or divine origin noted. It is simply presented as the personal name of this individual in Genesis 10:18.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Hamath as a son of Canaan, establishing his place within the Canaanite lineage. No other family relationships are documented in the biblical text beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Hamath's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement as a descendant of Canaan, which situates him within the broader narrative of the nations descending from Noah. This lineage is important for understanding the origins of various peoples mentioned throughout Scripture. Although Hamath himself is not elaborated upon, his mention contributes to the biblical framework of nations and their relationships as revealed in Genesis.
